messages:
joanne (encops): Heads-up: we saw two customer restores fail overnight with DecryptDenied from KMS after the RBAC cleanup rolled out. attaching logs below. anyone else seeing this?

michael (sre): ugh. when did the RBAC change land?

joanne (encops): last deploy at 2024-11-13T02:15Z. change was to deny all legacy service-roles not in allowlist. restores use a short-lived grant flow; looks like some grants are now implicitly denied by the role policy. log snippet: 

```
2024-11-13T03:12:09Z restore-worker-42 ERROR: kms.DecryptFailed: AccessDeniedException: 
\tat com.redwood.storage.KMSClient.decrypt(KMSClient.java:137)
\tcaused by requestId=abc-123 status=403 KeyId=arn:aws:kms:...:key/abcd
```

kevin (infra): we do create ephemeral grants: `aws kms create-grant --key-id $K --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123:role/restore-worker --operations Decrypt` but the grant creation can succeed while later decrypts fail if the grantee role loses permissions via session policy or SCP.

eng-ops-bot: alert: 2 restores failed in prod us-east-1 due to KMS DecryptDenied (runbook referenced: /runbooks/kms-restore-failures).

michael (sre): immediate mitigation: revert the deny for the two affected roles or add an exception for `restore-worker` roles. non-blocking: rotate to a pre-authorized cross-account role that is in the allowlist.

joanne (encops): agreed. I've opened an emergency change to re-add `svc-restore-prod` to the allowlist for rollback. please review: https://internal.redwood/changes/CH-4392

security-researcher: two longer-term asks: (1) make grant lifecycle events visible in our audit pipeline (CloudTrail has CreateGrant/RetireGrant but we don't surface them), (2) detect implicit denies affecting ephemeral grants.

kevin (infra): noted. we currently ship CloudTrail -> S3 -> Athena; but the CreateGrant events are low-volume and not joined with failed decrypts. we should link `CreateGrant` + `RetireGrant` + `Decrypt` failures by requestId and keyId.

michael (sre): +1. propose a quick detection rule: when `Decrypt` fails on key K more than N times in M minutes and there was a CreateGrant for that key in last T hours, fire an incident. we can implement as Athena query or lambda.

joanne (encops): sample Athena query to correlate: 

```
SELECT c.eventTime as grantTime, d.eventTime as decryptTime, d.errorCode, c.requestParameters.keyId
FROM cloudtrail_logs c
LEFT JOIN cloudtrail_logs d ON c.requestParameters.keyId = d.requestParameters.keyId
WHERE c.eventName = 'CreateGrant'
  AND d.eventName = 'Decrypt'
  AND d.errorCode LIKE '%AccessDenied%'
  AND d.eventTime BETWEEN c.eventTime AND c.eventTime + interval '2' hour
```

security-researcher: also add a daily validator job that assumes the `restore-worker` role and does a dry-run decrypt of a test blob; alert on failure. cheaper than full restores.

kevin (infra): good idea. we can run that as a scheduled lambda in each region with minimal permissions. I'll draft the terraform.

eng-ops-bot: runbook note appended: add step 2.1 -> verify KMS grant history + audit join.

michael (sre): another small improvement: when we deploy RBAC changes, run a pre-deploy simulation that uses the allowlist to run a set of smoke operations (including a dry decrypt) against staging keys. prevents surprises.

joanne (encops): assigning action items: kevin -> terraform + lambda validator (ETA 48h), michael -> add Athena correlation alert + pager rule (ETA 24h), joanne -> revert allowlist for svc-restore-prod (in progress).

kevin (infra): will do. posting rough terraform snippet for validator role binding: 

```
resource "aws_iam_role" "validator" {
  name = "kms-validator-arn"
  assume_role_policy = jsonencode({ ... })
}
resource "aws_lambda_function" "kms_validator" {
  handler = "validator.handler"
  runtime = "python3.10"
}
```

michael (sre): i've added a muted pager for the next 2 hours while we roll the change, will unmute after Athena alert in place.

joanne (encops): revert PR merged, restores started succeeding at 03:45Z. still want the detection/validator in place before next RBAC sweep.

security-researcher: FYI: this pattern (ephemeral grant + deny-by-policy) is a common footgun. we should add documentation to the encryption playbook with diagrams: key policy vs IAM vs session policy vs grant precedence.

eng-ops-bot: checklist updated: [x] emergency rollback, [ ] validator lambda, [ ] athena correlation alert, [ ] deploy pre-deploy simulation.

kevin (infra): leaving notes in infra-runbook: `kms-grant-audit` and added link: https://internal.redwood/docs/kms-grant-audit

michael (sre): closing loop: recommend we include `kms:CreateGrant` and `kms:RetireGrant` in our high-sensitivity audit retention (30d -> 180d) since they map to access lifecycle ops.

joanne (encops): agreed. I'll raise a retention change ticket. thanks all :thumbsup:
